items.title: Junior Mance Part II interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 18, 1999 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So I can work there with the quartet, you know the trio plus Joe, Joe Temperley.

ctx.x: Just a couple of things. I have noticed an awful lot of press, jazz is getting a lot of press lately. It seems like almost every week in the New York Times there’s some article about something. Has it translated to a better working situation do you think for musicians?

Well as far as New York there are more clubs. For the working situation, I think that’s something the union is going to address next, the clubs. For a lot of reasons the clubs aren’t paying the benefits or they’re behind on them, you know the pension fund and all that. Like you know the Broadway shows, the Broadway theaters do, and the studios naturally do, the recording companies. The clubs are the only ones. But that’s another subject altogether. As far as the music itself and playing, I think it’s better. I…

especially. But the club Zinno's is the club I work more than any other club. The owner is probably one of my best friends anyway. And it’s just around the corner from my house. I hang out in there a lot. They used to just do duos, but they moved the music room to the back, it’s bigger now, and they have groups. So I can work there with the quartet, you know the trio plus Joe, Joe Temperley. And it’s just a joy working there because there’s no, you know, watching the clock or anything.
